wu: Balloon Pop Review: Teacher holds 10 numbered balloons in different colors. Students take turns popping a balloon, saying its color and number (e.g., 'Blue, number 5!').
wuAlt: Color Hunt: Teacher calls out a color and number (e.g., '3 red balloons!'), students find matching flashcards and bring them to the front.
Number Jump: Students jump the number of times the teacher says, wearing a color hat (e.g., 'Jump 5 times if you have blue!').
pres: Teacher shows a map of Morocco with the Green March route. Models: 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color). Students repeat. Teacher holds up numbered flashcards and asks 'How many (red) flags?' Students answer 'Five red flags!'
presAlt: Flag Flashcards: Teacher shows Moroccan flag colors, says 'This is red and green.' Students repeat and point to colors on their mini-flags.
March Story: Teacher tells a short story about the Green March using a picture book, pointing to colors and numbers in the illustrations.
prac: Team Quiz Show: Two teams compete. Teacher asks 'How many (blue) balloons? Which one? The (big) one?' Teams buzz in, answer, and get points. Teacher supports with flashcards and gestures.
pracAlt: Color-by-Number: Students color a map of the Green March route using a worksheet with numbers (1=red, 2=green, etc.), saying 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color).'
Survey: Students ask classmates 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and tally answers on a simple bar graph.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a scene: 'There are 3 green flags and 2 red balloons. Draw them!' Students listen and draw, then check with a partner.
re: Color Relay: After break, students line up. Teacher calls 'Run to the (blue) circle!' Students race to touch the correct color, saying 'Blue! Number 4!'
prod: Map Craft: Students color a large map of the Green March route. In groups, they present: 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color). We see (number) flags!'
rw: Flag Writing: Students draw the Moroccan flag and write: 'The flag is red and green. There is a star.' Teacher helps with spelling and sentence structure.
st: Goodbye Song: 'Goodbye, Goodbye' with color and number actions (e.g., wave 3 times for 'green'). Sticker chart for participation, high-five line.
g: Teams buzz in to answer 'How many (color)? Which one?' questions for points.
Students color a map using number codes, saying 'The march goes to... (city name).'
Students ask 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and make a bar graph.
Students race to touch the correct color when called, saying 'Color! Number!'
Groups present their colored map, saying 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color).'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 quiz questions for a friend to answer.
Support: Use color/number word bank for writing and speaking tasks.
hw: Draw the Moroccan flag and write its colors in English.
Find a colors and numbers worksheet in the library folder and bring it done.
Ask your family 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and tell the class next week.
tip: Use the Green March theme to connect language learning to local history, making vocabulary memorable through cultural context.
